value.rationale: The Petersen line graph is a canonical 15-vertex vertex-transitive graph with a pre-established minimum zero-forcing size. Its full optimum configuration space, S5 symmetry types and exact exchange metric are natural unanswered enumerative/reconfiguration invariants. More than a count, the result identifies precisely the failure of Johnson-geodesic convexity: a sharp universal one-move additive detour bound with exactly 18,540 exceptional pairs. The explicit reproducible benchmark can test forcing reconfiguration algorithms and motivates structural generalizations; no general theorem is asserted.
